Histidine kinases (HKs) phosphorylate and dephosphorylate their… 1225513 specificity-residues-determine-binding-affinity-for-two-component-signal-transduction-systems specificity residues determine binding affinity two component signal UNLABELLED Two-component systems (TCS) comprise histidine kinases and their cognate response regulators an Specificity Residues Determine Binding Affinity for Two-Component Signal Transduction Systems UNLABELLED Two-component systems (TCS) comprise histidine kinases and their cognate response regulators and allow bacteria to sense and respond to a wide variety of signals. Histidine kinases (HKs) phosphorylate and dephosphorylate their cognate response regulators (RRs) in response to stimuli. In general, these reactions appear to be highly specific and require an appropriate association between the HK and RR proteins. The Myxococcus xanthus genome encodes one of the largest repertoires of signaling proteins in bacteria (685 open reading frames [ORFs]), including at least 127 HKs and at least 143 RRs.
